task.body: Add a property test in `test/tau/settings/loader_test.exs` verifying that `Tau.Settings.Loader` merge is commutative for non-conflicting keys and right-biased for conflicts, then make `mix test` pass.

implementer.diff:
diff --git a/test/tau/settings/loader_test.exs b/test/tau/settings/loader_test.exs
index 545db4d..0b934e5 100644
--- a/test/tau/settings/loader_test.exs
+++ b/test/tau/settings/loader_test.exs
@@ -1,8 +1,57 @@
 defmodule Tau.Settings.LoaderTest do
   use ExUnit.Case, async: true
+  use ExUnitProperties
 
   alias Tau.Settings.Loader
 
+  # Generators
+
+  # Scalar values: strings only (not maps, not lists) so merge_value falls through to right-bias.
+  defp scalar_gen, do: StreamData.string(:alphanumeric, min_length: 1)
+
+  # A list of scalars tagged as a non-list key so concatenation is not triggered.
+  # We generate flat maps with atom keys from a fixed pool to keep keys disjoint-able.
+  @pool_a [:alpha, :beta, :gamma, :delta]
+  @pool_b [:epsilon, :zeta, :eta, :theta]
+
+  defp flat_map_gen(key_pool) do
+    keys = StreamData.member_of(key_pool)
+
+    StreamData.map(
+      StreamData.list_of(
+        StreamData.tuple({keys, scalar_gen()}),
+        min_length: 1,
+        max_length: length(key_pool)
+      ),
+      &Map.new/1
+    )
+  end
+
+  describe "merge/2 properties" do
+    @tag :property
+    property "commutative for disjoint non-list-key scalar maps" do
+      check all(
+              a <- flat_map_gen(@pool_a),
+              b <- flat_map_gen(@pool_b)
+            ) do
+        assert Loader.merge(a, b) == Loader.merge(b, a)
+      end
+    end
+
+    @tag :property
+    property "right-biased for conflicting scalar keys" do
+      check all(
+              shared_key <- StreamData.member_of(@pool_a),
+              v_a <- scalar_gen(),
+              v_b <- scalar_gen()
+            ) do
+        a = %{shared_key => v_a}
+        b = %{shared_key => v_b}
+        assert Loader.merge(a, b)[shared_key] == v_b
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
   describe "merge/2" do
     test "later overrides earlier scalars" do
       assert Loader.merge(%{model: "a"}, %{model: "b"}) == %{model: "b"}
implementer.stdout_excerpt:
Two property tests added to `test/tau/settings/loader_test.exs`, both tagged `@tag :property`:

1. **Commutativity for disjoint keys** — generates maps with non-overlapping atom key sets and asserts `merge(a, b) == merge(b, a)`.
2. **Right-bias for conflicts** — generates a shared key with two scalar values and asserts `merge(a, b)[key] == b[key]`.

Suite result: 360 tests, 0 failures. One formatting snag was hit (`check all` needs parenthesized form under Elixir 1.18) and fixed before the format gate passed.

findings.message: Commutativity property uses disjoint key pools that exclude all list_keys(), making it a tautology. For disjoint maps, Map.merge is always commutative regardless of Loader logic. The property will never catch a regression in merge_value/3 because no conflict path is exercised.
findings.evidence: @pool_a and @pool_b contain no overlap with list_keys() ([:hooks,:extensions,:mcp,:allow,:deny,:ask,:permissions]). With disjoint inputs Map.merge(a,b)==Map.merge(b,a) holds by definition; Loader.merge reduces to Map.merge with no conflict callbacks fired. The OTP non-negotiable #6 (properties before examples for invariant-bearing modules) requires that the property actually exercise the invariant, not sidestep it.

findings.message: The property suite does not cover the merge_value/3 branches for nested maps or list-key concatenation. list_keys() contains 7 keys; none appear in any generator. A refactor that swaps v1 and v2 in the list concatenation path (turning right-append into left-append) would leave both new properties green.
findings.evidence: lib/tau/settings/loader.ex:43-48 — merge_value for list-keys does v1 ++ v2; this is the only place Loader.merge differs from Map.merge. Neither property generates inputs that reach this branch. The spec-before-code rule requires tests that fail before the change and pass after; a property that cannot fail on a regression does not satisfy that gate.

findings.message: Right-bias property uses StreamData.member_of(@pool_a) for the shared key but @pool_a keys are not in list_keys(), so the test only covers the scalar fallthrough branch. Consider also generating keys from list_keys() and verifying that non-list values at those keys remain right-biased, and that list values at those keys do NOT satisfy the right-bias assertion (they concatenate instead), to document the distinction explicitly.
findings.evidence: lib/tau/settings/loader.ex:43-51 — two distinct behaviours for list-keyed vs non-list-keyed conflicting values.
